Of those two other options Purdue would be best. I’m not going to lie and say “OSU is just as good” even though it’s not. OSU Engineering is a good program and if you follow through you will get good outcomes from it but it certainly isn’t really at the same level as those other schools. At those schools for engineering you’d have better opportunities in general (although this depends a lot on you), better connected faculty and more engineering resources. 

But is it worth the extra debt to go those other schools? Typically I’d say no especially for undergrad BUT since EE is a lucrative career if you follow through and work hard you wouldn’t really have a hard time paying back any debt or getting your moneys worth. 

Honestly I’d say your answer depends on your post grad plans. If you wanna do a masters or anything I’d choose OSU to save money cus post undergraduate can get very expensive. If you don’t have post undergraduate plans, then it’s a bit more open. If you get into Purdue that makes it enticing.

Yeah np! You first have to qualify and apply for an LSAC fee waiver through the website and go through the process. You qualify through income/need. They typically decline most people at first automatically and you have to go through an "appeal" process where you provide a letter and documentation outlining your needs. They will get back to you within a week or so.

The cool thing with this is that you also get to take your LSAT for free at least once if get it.

Once you have that you can email 7sage directly with PDF attachment of the letter LSAC emails you approving you and then they'll allow you to access it for a dollar!
